key_insight: Big-means++ turns repeated K-means runs on randomly sampled surrogate datasets into a data-native global search strategy for big-data clustering, aiming to escape poor local minima without expensive metaheuristic hybrids.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable way to cluster very large or arbitrarily tall datasets using only finite samples, making it practical for high-volume scientific and industrial data pipelines.
method: Flowing-incumbent K-means refinements carry centroid states across fresh sampled landscapes instead of resetting to a best-so-far solution.
Geometric sample-size shaking explores multiple resolution scales and helps handle cluster imbalance.
A multi-agent asynchronous search runs independent trajectories with automatic convergence detection for speed-quality control.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on 22 datasets against 11 competing algorithms, showing effectiveness, efficiency, and robustness.
watch_item: Because the method relies on stochastic sampling and surrogate landscapes, performance may depend on sample-size schedules, stopping criteria, and random initialization settings.
paper_title: Data-Native Global Optimization for Big Data K-means Clustering
